## Start here: the 5 rules

1. **Type the formula with no spaces in it, then press Space.** The whole formula changes at once.
2. **Commands start with a backslash** `\`: `\alpha` gives α, `\int` gives ∫.
3. **`^` raises, `_` lowers.** One character: `x^2`, `x_1`. More than one: use braces `x^{n+1}` or brackets `x^(n+1)`.
4. **Braces `{ }` group things.** `\sqrt{x+1}` puts the whole of x+1 under the root; `\frac{a}{b}` is a over b.
5. **Made a mistake?** Press Backspace straight away to get back exactly what you typed.

> ✱ marks formulas longer than 25 characters. They need one extra line in Espanso's `config/default.yml`: `max_regex_buffer_size: 64` (run `espanso path config` to find the folder). Without it they stay as typed.

> Tip: want a space *inside* a formula? Type `~` (or `\,` for a thin space). Want spaces *around* operators? Put real spaces there: `A \cup B` gives `A ∪ B`.

## Superscripts and subscripts

| Type | You get | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x^2` | x² | single character |
| `x^10` | x¹⁰ | a whole number |
| `x^{n+1}` | xⁿ⁺¹ | group with braces |
| `x^(n+1)` | xⁿ⁺¹ | or with brackets, PowerPoint style |
| `x^{-1}` | x⁻¹ | negative power |
| `x_1` | x₁ | subscript |
| `a_{ij}` | aᵢⱼ | two-letter subscript |
| `x_n^2` | xₙ² | both at once |
| `\alpha_1` | α₁ | on a command |
| `{a+b}^2` | (a+b)² | on a group: brackets are added |
| `e^{-x^2}` | e⁻ˣ² | nested |
| `A^T` | Aᵀ | transpose |
| `f^\prime` | f′ | prime |
| `90^\circ` | 90° | degrees |
| `v_y` | v\_y | no Unicode subscript y: stays readable |

**Characters that can be raised:** ()+-0123456789=ABDEGHIJKLMNOPRTUVWabcdefghijklmnoprstuvwxyz and Greek αβγδεϵθιφϕχ.  
**Characters that can be lowered:** ()+-0123456789=aehijklmnoprstuvx and Greek əβγρφϕχ.  
Anything else is written in linear form, e.g. `v_y`, `e^(iπ)`, `lim_(x→0)`. This is a limit of Unicode itself.

## Fractions

Unicode cannot stack a fraction, so fractions are written on one line. Vulgar fractions: `1/2` ½, `1/3` ⅓, `2/3` ⅔, `1/4` ¼, `3/4` ¾, `1/5` ⅕, `2/5` ⅖, `3/5` ⅗, `4/5` ⅘, `1/6` ⅙, `5/6` ⅚, `1/7` ⅐, `1/8` ⅛, `3/8` ⅜, `5/8` ⅝, `7/8` ⅞, `1/9` ⅑, `1/10` ⅒, `0/3` ↉.

| Type | You get | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `\frac{1}{2}` | ½ | common fraction |
| `\frac12` | ½ | short form |
| `1/2` | ½ | typed directly |
| `\frac{3}{16}` | ³⁄₁₆ | any numbers |
| `\frac{a}{b}` | a/b | letters |
| `\frac{a+b}{c}` | (a+b)/c | brackets added when needed |
| `\frac{1}{2\pi}` | 1/(2π) |  |
| `\frac{dy}{dx}` | dy/dx | derivatives stay clean |
| `\frac{a}{b}^2` | (a/b)² | power of a fraction |
| `\dfrac{a}{b}` | a/b | \dfrac, \tfrac, \cfrac work too |
| `\binom{n}{k}` | ⁿCₖ | binomial coefficient |

## Negation with \not

Put `\not` before a relation to cross it out.

| Type | You get | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `\not=` | ≠ | not equal |
| `\not<` | ≮ | not less-than |
| `\not>` | ≯ | not greater-than |
| `\not\in` | ∉ | is not an element of |
| `\not\subset` | ⊄ | not a subset of |
| `\not\subseteq` | ⊈ | neither a subset of nor equal to |
| `\not\equiv` | ≢ | not identical to |
| `\not\sim` | ≁ | not tilde |
| `\not\cong` | ≇ | neither approximately nor actually equal to |
| `\not\approx` | ≉ | not almost equal to |
| `\not\exists` | ∄ | there does not exist |
| `\not\mid` | ∤ | does not divide |
| `\not\parallel` | ∦ | not parallel to |
| `\not\to` | ↛ | rightwards arrow with stroke |
| `\not\Rightarrow` | ⇏ | rightwards double arrow with stroke |

These work inside any formula. The longest one always wins, so `<=>` is never mistaken for `<=`.

| `...` | … | horizontal ellipsis |
| `<--` | ⟵ | long leftwards arrow |
| `<->` | ↔ | left right arrow |
| `<==` | ⟸ | long leftwards double arrow |
| `<=>` | ⇔ | if and only if |
| `===` | ≡ | identical / congruent mod |
| `==>` | ⟹ | long rightwards double arrow |
| `\|->` | ↦ | maps to |
| `!=` | ≠ | not equal |
| `+-` | ± | plus-minus |
| `-+` | ∓ | minus-plus |
| `->` | → | to / maps to / tends to |
| `/<` | ≮ | not less-than |
| `/=` | ≠ | not equal |
| `/>` | ≯ | not greater-than |
| `:=` | ≔ | colon equals |

## Function names

Written upright, with a thin space before a following letter, as in printed maths: `\sin\theta` gives sin θ, `\log_2{n}` gives log₂ n.

`\arccos`, `\arccosh`, `\arccot`, `\arccsc`, `\arcosh`, `\arcsec`, `\arcsin`, `\arcsinh`, `\arctan`, `\arctanh`, `\arg`, `\argmax`, `\argmin`, `\arsinh`, `\artanh`, `\bmod`, `\cos`, `\cosh`, `\cot`, `\coth`, `\Cov`, `\csc`, `\csch`, `\deg`, `\det`, `\diag`, `\dim`, `\erf`, `\erfc`, `\exp`, `\gcd`, `\hom`, `\inf`, `\ker`, `\lcm`, `\lg`, `\lim`, `\liminf`, `\limsup`, `\ln`, `\log`, `\max`, `\min`, `\mod`, `\Pr`, `\rank`, `\sec`, `\sech`, `\sgn`, `\sin`, `\sinh`, `\span`, `\sup`, `\tan`, `\tanh`, `\tr`, `\Tr`, `\trace`, `\Var`

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happened.** Did you press Space? Conversion happens on Space, not Enter. Is there a space inside the formula? Remove it.

**A long formula stayed exactly as typed (formulas marked ✱).** Long formulas need a bigger buffer: add `max_regex_buffer_size: 64` to Espanso's `config/default.yml`. Without it, formulas up to 25 characters convert.

**`v_y` or `x^q` stayed as typed.** Unicode has no subscript y or superscript q. That is the readable fallback, not an error.

**`a<->b` became `←>`, or text vanished.** LibreOffice's own AutoCorrect got there first. See *Step 4* in the README.

**Symbols look like a different font.** Your font lacks them. See *Fonts* in the README, or use DejaVu Sans.

**I wanted the raw text back.** Press Backspace immediately after the conversion.

**A command is missing.** Add it yourself in `USER_SYMBOLS` in `generate_rules.py`, or open an issue on GitHub.
